shortName: The Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: In accordance with our mission of educating culturally competent physicians, the curriculum incorporates content on gender, race and ethnicity in medicine, implicit bias, LGBTQ healthcare, and disability healthcare for all students. Students may opt to pursue more in-depth projects in these areas through pre-clerkship electives, the Scholarly Concentrations Program, or independent study. Alpert Medical School invites applications from individuals that share the cultural and experiential diversity of those the healthcare field serves.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may apply for time off from academic activities for a variety of personal and professional reasons. The Student Affairs Handbook provides details on types of leave and procedural obligations and may accessed on the AMS website.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Medical Student Senate sponsors over 85 groups focused in areas of medical/community advocacy, professional associations, education, service, and medical specialties. Those interested in the performing arts may join the The Providence Medical Orchestra, or participate in "Musicale: a Community Concert by and for students, residents and physicians," or the student run "Low Yield" show. Healing for Harmony is a student group that offers performances in health care and community settings. Students also participate in a wide variety of community outreach programs, including two local free medical clinics and well-established prisoner health initiatives. A health and wellness program based in the fourth floor exercise rooms (with fully equipped gym) includes yoga, meditation, and other group activities. Students enjoy access to the full range of athletic clubs and other activities of Brown University.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The medical education building is located in the historic Jewelry District of Providence, less than a mile from Brown's main campus and within walking distance of several laboratories, research facilities and several affiliated hospitals. Providence's many restaurants, theaters, shopping, and river walk are easily accessible on foot. The nearby Rhode Island School of Design offers both a world-class museum and classes in photography, sculpture and painting.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Affordable housing options are available in several historic neighborhoods within walking/biking distance of the medical education building. The Auxiliary Housing Office leases and manages about 150 residential housing units in the vicinity. Monthly rents range from $935 to $1,300 in Brown-owned housing.  The Providence area also offers a mixed range of privately owned properties from spartan studio rentals to luxurious high rise condos and small and large private homes.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Support systems for gender and sexual minority students are overseen by the  Office of Belonging, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, in conjunction with the Office of Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Wellness services and programming at Brown is multi-dimensional and encompasses physical, emotional and social activities to help students maintain a positive attitude and lifestyle. Ongoing wellness programs and events are scheduled periodically throughout the academic year to enhance the social and emotional well-being of students. Efforts are overseen by a Chief Wellness Officer and include ongoing general wellness programming, longitudinal mentoring, dedicated therapy services for Medical Students through Brown's Counseling and Psychological Services, and a Learning Specialist who works specifically with medical students.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Warren Alpert Medical School, in keeping with Brown University's mission and values, supports a collaborative culture of mutual respect, encourages interdisciplinary learning, and is dedicated to social responsibility and community engagement, both locally and globally.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: While a car is not a requirement the majority of students do choose to keep a car. The expense of car ownership is not as much as it would be in larger cities. Brown University Shuttles are available, and Brown University students enjoy free access to RI public transportation.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Medical Education provides tutoring services for medical students at any point during the semester. Specific tutoring assignments for individuals and groups are available upon request.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Clinical work with patients begins M1 though a pre-clerkship clinical skills and  professional development course called Doctoring. Local free-clinics provide additional opportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures, laboratory sessions, small group learning sessions, Team-based learning, and simulation (with standardized patients for clinical skills training) in Years I and II.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin February of M2. Most students rotate through the core clerkships at our affiliated hospitals. PC-PM dual-degree students participate in an integrated longitudinal clerkship.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at lectures is generally not mandatory. Lectures are available online.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Pre-clerkship training is structured within two longitudinal courses: Integrated Medical Sciences (IMS) and Doctoring. IMS starts with  Scientific Foundations of Medicine, Histology, Anatomy, General Pathology, and Health Systems Science, followed by systems-based science courses for the remainder of pre-clerkship training: Brain Sciences, Supporting Structures–Rheumatology, Orthopedics and Dermatology–,Microbiology and Infectious Diseases, Cardiovascular, Pulmonary, Renal, Endocrinology, Human Reproduction, Hematology, and Gastroenterology. Doctoring I-IV provides clinical skills training plus community-based clinical skills teaching with physician mentors. Students in the third and fourth years complete 44 weeks of clinical clerkships (internal medicine, surgery, psychiatry/clinical neuroscience, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, family medicine), and 36 weeks of electives, a sub-internship, and a surgical or surgery-related elective.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Alpert Medical School has a longstanding commitment to training physicians who will provide health care to all segments of the population. This commitment is underscored by the centrality of the Doctoring course throughout the curriculum, which pairs many students with community primary care physicians.  With the support of grant funding from the NIH and the Rhode Island Foundation, the school has enhanced the clinical curriculum and the Scholarly Concentrations program to expand our focus on healthcare delivery to the under-served, population health, and health policy.  The Primary Care-Population Medicine program, for a subset of students, focuses on tenets of primary care and population medicine. Students have the option of volunteering within two local free clinics, with Brown University's Center for Prisoner Health and Human Rights, and the school's Global Health Initiative, among many other programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Brown University's Division of Biology and Medicine sponsors many research programs within the affiliated teaching hospitals and in facilities on or near Brown's campus and the Medical School campus, which are in walking distance of each other. Research areas include bioengineering, including dynamic collaborations between orthopedics and engineering; brain science, from the neuronal to behavioral level; and pediatrics and perinatal biology, including foci in autism, asthma, and obesity. Other opportunities involve community-based research with faculty in all areas of clinical practice, and international research in any of the 33 countries in which Brown faculty are conducting studies under the auspices of the Global Health Initiative. Biomedical research opportunities can be augmented through collaborative interactions with the Brown Center for Biomedical Informatics.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Not required, but many opportunities exist for significant community involvement, including service work in local free health clinics, prisoner health initiatives, and educational outreach programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: 96% of graduating students reported a research project with a faculty member, 83% reported completion of an independent study project for credit, and 82% reported authorship of a peer-reviewed paper.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Bradley, Butler, Hasbro Children's, Hope Health, Kent Hospital, Providence VA Medical Center, Rhode Island Hospital, The Miriam Hospital, Women and Infants Hospital of Rhode Island.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Grading in the pre-clerkship curriculum is pass/fail (Satisfactory/Non Credit). Honors, Satisfactory and Non Credit are used in the third year clerkships and fourth year clinical electives.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Since granting its first Doctor of Medicine degrees in 1975, The Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University has become a national leader in medical education and biomedical research. Housed in a 110,000 square-foot medical education building located between main campus and the principle teaching hospitals, Alpert Medical School sits at the heart of a growing biomedical and innovation hub in downtown Providence and is the only medical school in Rhode Island, serving not only RI but into southern Massachusetts.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: To support and promote the health of individuals and communities through innovative medical education programs, research initiatives, and clinical excellence in service to society and to improve the health and wellness of all.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: Brown’s Program in Liberal Medical Education (PLME) combines undergraduate education and professional studies in medicine in a single eight-year program. The PLME is the only combined baccalaureate-MD program in the Ivy League, providing one route of admission to the Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks to acknowledge offer to hold a seat in the class until April 30. Waitlist offers are assigned individual response dates.
medSchoolApplication.matricNote: Note: Acceptance/Matriculation Data includes applications and matriculants via the Program in Liberal Medical Education (PLME).
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Committee packets count as one letter.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Thursdays and most Fridays between mid-September and February.  The interview day program runs from 9:40am until 3:30pm and includes an orientation session, virtual tour led by a current student, student lunchtime panel, and two 30 minute one-on-one open file interviews.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Group session and two individual meetings.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: After the receipt of an email invitation to complete the secondary. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. Applications with pending MCAT scores are reviewed after scores are received.

medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: All applicants can apply, but financial aid is limited.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: All applicants can apply, but financial aid is limited.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
COVID-19 - Information for 2026 Admissions Cycle
Pass/Fail Coursework:  Acknowledging the challenges brought by COVID, For coursework during or after Spring 2020 and through Spring 2022, AMS will accept pass/fail and on-line coursework, even for prerequisite courses. Passing the course will satisfy our requirement, whether pass/fail or graded. Candidates should consider that academic aptitude in the sciences is one among a number of factors considered in selecting students, so a graded option when available may be preferable for those with limited science coursework. 

MCAT scores are required for the standard AMCAS route of admissions.

The Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University considers a maximum of three (3) application attempts.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are considered as one among many factors in a holistic review process.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee considers applications showing a minimum grade point average of 3.0, including all undergraduate coursework, even if taken after completion of the primary baccalaureate degree. Graduate level coursework is considered separately.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: 3.0 is the minimum undergraduate gpa to be considered for admission. While there is no cut-off above this gpa, the average gpa for admitted candidates generally falls between 3.6 and 3.8 with a wider range.  Admitted candidates with an undergraduate gpa at the lower end of the range have usually completed postbacc or graduate level coursework showing an upward trend in academic achievement over time. All coursework taken after the undergraduate program, whether postbacc or at the graduate level is considered.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All coursework taken at any level is considered in reviewing an applicant's readiness to begin medical school. Successful candidates with undergraduate work at the lower end of the academic range have usually completed postbacc or graduate level coursework showing an upward trend in academic achievement over time. There is no minimum number of hours of post-graduate work to be considered, but coursework sufficient to demonstrate a student's current academic readiness, particularly in the sciences, is required.  This will be different for different for different candidates, depending on their particular academic record, gpa trend, and time since the completion of their undergraduate degree.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community College coursework is acceptable to fulfill individual prerequisite requirements. Success in additional or more advanced coursework at a 4-year bachelor's level school or above will enhance a candidate's competitiveness in the application process.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants have the option to upload up to two documents through the applicant portal, and can send additional updates to the admissions office by email. Updates are not required and may or may not be reviewed. Candidates placed on the waitlist are encouraged to update their file if they have not already done so.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Alpert Medical School assists students in meeting educational expenses with financial aid packages that consist of low-interest loans and need-based institutional grants. 66% percent of all students received financial aid in 2024-25, with $12.5 million allocated in need and merit-based scholarship, with an average scholarship amount $43,410
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The annual tuition amount is determined by the Corporation of the University for a given academic year.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
MD/PhD:  A small cohort of medical students pursue an MD/PhD course of study.  Although not currently funded through the Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP), the MD/PhD Program provides for tuition remission for both the medical school and graduate program years, as well as a stipend during the graduate school years.

MD/MPH:  Once matriculated, current students can apply to pursue an accelerated MD/MPH at Brown University School of Public Health after the second year of medical school. https://mph.sph.brown.edu/concentrations/accelerated

MD-ScM:  Applicants who complete the Warren Alpert Medical School Secondary Application can elect to be considered for a special concurrently earned MD-ScM dual-degree in Primary Care and Population Medicine. Applicants must be admitted to the MD Program prior to consideration for the dual-degree option with that program. Interested applicants still choose Regular MD in AMCAS.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: Varies from year to year, usually between 10-30.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Candidates placed on the waitlist are encouraged to update their file if they have not already done so.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: All required coursework must be completed prior to matriculation. On a case-by-case basis, competency may be demonstrated by more advanced coursework, research or employment in the field.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Required coursework completed within prior 10 years is considered. On a case-by-case basis, competency may be demonstrated by more advanced coursework, research or employment in the field.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Selection criteria include academic achievement, faculty evaluations, and evidence of maturity, leadership, integrity, and compassion. Eligible candidates present a minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.00 (4.00 scale) in undergraduate courses. Premedical requirements must be completed at an accredited US or Canadian institution of higher learning. Applicants must complete baccalaureate degree requirements before matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Clinical experience is required. This exposure can be achieved in a number of ways: shadowing; volunteer or paid work as a scribe, EMT, or paraprofessional (CNA, RN, etc.); volunteer work in a hospital or other clinical setting, or volunteer or paid clinical research work that includes significant interaction with patients.
